title: Pass every time
eyebrow: CETI · a data film · agents, one try versus every try
lede: A field of 460 cubes, one per try, lit about 60 percent: the picture of an agent that is usually right. Turn the field and the same cubes stand as 115 columns, one per task: only 44 are lit all the way. Then the same move on 296 pull requests that pass the tests, and on the length of task an agent can do reliably.

captions: A usually-right agent does most of the work.
Or does it? Count every try, task by task.
Customer service: GPT-4o on tau-bench retail.
115 tasks. One tile each.
Four tries per task: 460 cubes.
278 passed. A lit cube is a pass.
Tries that pass: 60.4 %.
Now turn the field. Each task becomes a column.
Judge a task by all its tries, not by one.
Sort the same columns by how many tries passed.
44 tasks pass all four tries.
22 never pass.
Cut the field at all four tries.
All four tries pass: 38.3 %.
Count one try at a time: 60.4 %.
Count each task by all four tries: 38.3 %.
Same cubes, two answers. Which one was quoted?
The paper's own 8-try run: under 25 %.
A pass rate averages tries. Every time is per task.
Passing a benchmark is not the same as shipping.
296 PRs pass the tests.
Top SWE-bench Verified score: 80.9 %.
4 maintainers read them. Would they merge?
About half would not be merged.
Another agent, another yardstick: task length.
At the 80 % bar: 27 min.
4 h 49 min at the 50 % bar.
About 10 times longer than at the 80 % bar.
On Monday, ask for the every-time number.

brand.takeaway: A pass is not a pass every time.
